verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is community comments listing 'code owners' and 'protected branches' as GitHub features, which are lost on private repos when downgrading to Free. This shows the product has a code-owners capability, but nothing documents how required approvals for owned paths actually work. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the CODEOWNERS file and path-to-owner mapping, documentation that branch protection can require code-owner approval before merge, hands-on corroboration that enforcement works, and clarity on plan availability for public versus private repos.

support.subject: As an open-source-maintainer, I can require approval from designated code owners for changes to the paths they own
